newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MAIZE DOWN, MILLING WHEAT UP IN SLOW BUDAPEST MKT.
newsitem.headline: MAIZE DOWN, MILLING WHEAT UP IN SLOW BUDAPEST MKT.

text.p: Milling wheat futures mostly rose while maize finished lower after a slow day in the grains section of the Budapest Commodity Exchange, dealers said on Monday.
Contracts maturing in March bucked the downward trend of maize futures, rising 300 forints to 17,700 forints per tonne.
"With the physical market's prices around 18,000 forints, delivery is not really possible at current price levels," said Istvan Grebats of Termin Broker.
May delivery maize ended at 16,900 forints, down 100, while new (1997) crop prices finished between 16,910 forints for July and 18,400 for December.
"There is a tendency among market players to close open positions for the new maize crop, but only if that can be done at reasonable prices," Grebats said.
Milling wheat for May closed at 24,410 forints, down 390, due to selling pressure, he added.
Feed barley prices rose by the 400-forints daily limit for all maturities, rising above milling wheat prices for the corresponding months.
"This shows that there just isn't enough barley around," Grebats said.
Feed barley finished between 27,720 forints for March to 19,800 for September, but there were only two contracts traded for the March maturity.
Total turnover was a meagre 208.97 million forints or 556 contracts, of which 324 were for maize.
Lot size is 20,000 kgs for all contracts.
